growth_stages.notes: Comparatively heat-tolerant relative to flowering; not a focus of the cited literature.
Flowering (anthesis/fertilization) is the most heat-sensitive stage in rice. Sterility is caused by poor anther dehiscence and low pollen production/germination.
growth_stages.reference_detail: Spikelets exposed to temperatures >35C for as little as ~1 hour at anthesis show increased sterility; classic literature reports >35C for ~5 days causes complete sterility. A lower threshold of 33C for spikelet sterility has also been reported (genotype-dependent).
sources: Jagadish et al., J. Exp. Bot. 58(7):1627 (2007) - https://academic.oup.com/jxb/article/58/7/1627/512931
Field-level evaluation of rice ILs for heat tolerance, PMC4938818 - https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4938818/
Satake & Yoshida 1978, cited in Jagadish et al. 2007
Bheemanahalli et al. 2016 (33C threshold), cited in secondary source

growth_stages.notes: Heat during grain filling reduces harvest index and grain quality, though less catastrophically than flowering-stage sterility.
sources: Prasad et al., Field Crops Research 95:398-411 (2006)

engine_notes: 35C/short-duration is the most frequently replicated threshold across the cited studies for rice flowering; some genotypes show sterility onset closer to 33C. CropHeat treats 35C as the default engine threshold and documents the 33C variant as genotype-dependent uncertainty, not a hidden assumption.
